header.sector: Consumer electronics and devices (PCs, notebooks, phones, displays)
header.title: Consumer memory demand weak as cost pass-through squeezes PC and mobile end markets

s01_bottom_line.text: Rising memory costs weigh on PC notebook end-market sales and suppress smartphone production/bit demand, with PC brands reducing SSD capacities and smartphone brands relying on inventories, limiting incremental procurement.
Consumer-side demand (PC, mobile, TV) remains weak and pressured by higher memory costs even as AI-driven segments drive prices up.
Higher memory component costs are pressuring consumer device makers' margins and demand, a negative read-through for PC and smartphone OEMs, though the article quantifies no earnings impact.

items.text: Rising costs and depletion of low-cost inventories weigh on smartphone production, suppressing overall mobile DRAM bit demand.
PC brands are reducing SSD capacities in mainstream models to lower BOM costs, declining procurement volumes and per-device capacity.
Smartphone brands rely on existing inventories, leaving very limited incremental eMMC/UFS procurement.
The NAND Flash market shows a divergence between accelerating AI demand and weak consumer demand.
In eMMC/UFS, OEMs are purchasing only minimum volumes needed to maintain supplier relationships, narrowing negotiations to price confirmation for small order volumes.
